assertions.name: closed_form_pair_counts_match_brute_force
assertions.note: min(Z,d,N,A-d) for the p-n census is the step that could quietly be wrong; this is the control that says it is not

assertions.name: full_range_over_binds_relative_to_contact
assertions.note: the implied scale moves by 1.90427x. The contact chain already over-binds at 0.886, so this was the expected direction and is NOT the test -- see section 2

assertions.name: full_range_moves_p5_p95_down_but_the_full_spread_UP
assertions.note: p5-p95 1.224972733 -> 1.207270092 (1.445 % better) but full 10.18150685 -> 10.70821279 (5.173 % worse). One measure improving marginally while the widest worsens is redistribution, not repair

assertions.name: and_layout_free_bond_counting_still_beats_both
assertions.note: layout-free (A-1) scores p5-p95 1.180845597, full 8.173443606 -- better than full range on BOTH. Restoring the range does not recover what the isospin-resolved letters cost in the first place (qou-q7ga)

assertions.name: the_range_extension_moves_the_LIGHT_end_not_the_heavy_one
assertions.note: scale-normalised median shifts 6.9354 % in A=2-20 against -0.545835 % in the heaviest bin. Light nuclei have few pairs, so extending the range changes them most in relative terms -- and they are where the tails of the distribution live

assertions.name: full_range_washes_out_the_layout_difference
assertions.note: segregated-vs-alternating p5-p95 gap 0.4589 % at contact, -0.03037 % at full range. Once every pair contributes, the ORDER of the nucleons stops mattering -- an independent route to qou-48is's finding

parameters.identification: mu = -ln b -- a MODELLING CHOICE, not derived; the same b that suppresses the trace per bond is taken to set the range
